text:
B: Hello! There we go. How are you doing? How's your day been?
A: Oh, erm, hiya. Yeah, alright, thanks. Bit knackered. Can you hear me okay?
B: Loud and clear. I'm Gareth, by the way.
A: Joanne. Sorry, I never know how to start these.
B: No, you're fine, I'm making it up as I go too. Why knackered? Long day?
A: Three twelve-hour shifts on the trot. I'm a senior care assistant, residential home near Huntingdon. I run the day shift, so meds, handovers, the rota, all of it.
B: Three twelves, blimey. And then you sign up for this.
A: I know. I must be mad. What do you do?
B: I'm a teacher, geography, secondary school in Maidstone. And Head of Year 9, which is basically, er, sort of half teaching and half sorting out who said what on Snapchat.
A: Year 9. Oh, I don't envy you that.
B: Honestly, I love them. They're daft but they're good kids, mostly. Same as your residents, probably, you get fond of them.
A: Yeah, you do. Some of them you really do. And then when one goes downhill it, you know, it gets you. You're not supposed to let it, but it does.
B: Yeah. Yeah, I can imagine. My dad had a stroke a couple of years back, so I see a bit of that world now. The carers who come in to him are brilliant. Proper unsung heroes, mate. Sorry, calling you mate, I do that.
A: No, you're alright. And thank you. Most people don't think about it till it's their own mum or dad.
B: That's exactly it. Till it's your own.
A: Is he alright now, your dad?
B: Up and down. I drive over to Ashford most weekends to help my mum. M20 permitting.
A: Oh, don't talk to me about roads. The A14 roadworks are a nightmare. It's been years.
B: Years! Ours too. They just move the cones about to look busy, I reckon.
A: That's what Darren says, my husband. He's a delivery driver, so he's on it all day moaning.
B: Ha, I bet. Have you got kids at home?
A: Callum, he's seventeen, doing plumbing at college. And Ellie, she's twenty, moved out. And Bella, she's our staffie. She's getting old, dodgy hip.
B: Oh bless her. We've got a Labrador, Biscuit, very old, very lazy. Ate half a loaf off the counter on Sunday. Whole thing, wrapper and all nearly.
A: No! Labradors, honestly. Bella just steals Callum's toast, but he leaves his plates everywhere so that's his own fault.
B: So what do you do to switch off, after twelve hours?
A: Telly, mainly. Corrie, Strictly. I have Strictly on every Saturday without fail, cup of tea, nobody talks to me. And we still go to the panto at Christmas. Started when the kids were little and now we just, we just keep going.
B: No way. I do the staff panto at school. Three years running. Last year I was the dame.
A: You never. In the dress and everything?
B: Full wig, mate. Kids have never let me forget it. Sorry, I'm rambling a bit there.
A: No, that's made me laugh. Is there a photo? Bet there's a photo somewhere on—
